Subject: Surge -> Slate transition: bundling questions and rollback window

Hi Jonas,

We’re exploring moving Surgetech’s fleet from the current Surge plan up to Slate for the higher throughput and quantization options. Before we commit, procurement has two main asks:

- A short (preferably 30-day) rollback window from the pilot upgrade where we can return to our previous plan without penalty if performance/latency or cost outcomes don’t meet expectations.
- A clear mapping of feature parity: which current Surge features are included in Slate versus which would be sold as add-ons (private VPC, audit log retention, expanded KV cache limits).

I attached a small usage export for May so you can see our token profile and burst characteristics (surgetech-usage-may.csv). Can you put together 1) a recommended packaging path (upgrade vs addon) and 2) the commercial terms we should expect for a 30-day pilot? We’d also like to know if any discounts or stepdown credits apply if we return to Surge after the pilot.

Heather

Subject: Re: Surge -> Slate transition: bundling questions and rollback window

Hi Heather,

Thanks for the usage slice 1 looks helpful. High-level: Slate is designed for throughput-first customers and covers most of the features you mentioned, but a couple of things are commonly sold as configurable add-ons. Attach: Slate_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing + feature map).

Two practical packaging routes:

1) Full Slate upgrade (recommended if you need sustained throughput):
   - Slate includes higher throughput pool, expanded KV cache by default, and our latency SLOs.
   - Private VPC and extended audit retention are add-ons (flat monthly fee).
   - Typical per-token rate: $0.0012/token for standard quantized variants (pilot rate below).

2) Surge + Slate Add-on (recommended if you want minimal change):
   - Keep Surge core, add Slate throughput pack for peak windows and the private VPC add-on.
   - Slightly higher effective per-token for bursts but preserves current billing mechanics.

Commercial suggestion for a 30-day pilot:
- Pilot discount: 10% off the Slate per-token rate for the pilot period.
- Rollback window: 30 calendar days from go-live. If you elect to step back within the window, no retrospective usage charge changes; we will honor the original Surge invoicing for the rollback period and provide a one-time credit equal to the pilot discount differential.
- If you keep Slate after 30 days, standard Slate rates apply moving forward.

Next steps I propose: I can draft a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with dates and success criteria. Kimberly / Ben / Lauren: can you confirm finance and legal comfort with the rollback credit language and the 10% pilot discount?

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Internal note - copying pricing: we can accept the 10% pilot discount and the 30-day rollback credit, but need finance sign-off for the exact credit mechanics (one-time credit vs invoice adjustment) and final DocuSign language.

Suggested risk controls:
- Pilot as a scoped migration: only 40% of production traffic routed to Slate for first 14 days, then review KPIs (latency P90, token cost delta, error rates).
- If metrics pass, widen to 100% for remaining 16 days of pilot period.
- Rollback path: automatic routing back to Surge if latency > SLA or error rate > baseline + 1.5x during pilot (we should define measurement windows).

Lauren: please confirm finance OK to credit back the discount differential as a one-time line item instead of re-billing historical usage (simpler for procurement).

1) MAP: please send a 3-line Mutual Action Plan we can insert into our SOW. Example we’d prefer:
   - 5/29 go-live (40% traffic to Slate), 6/12 review, 6/15 full traffic if KPIs met;
   - Success criteria: P90 latency delta <= +20ms, token cost delta <= +8% compared to Surge baseline, error rate <= baseline + 1.5x;
   - Rollback mechanism and crediting: if we step back before 6/22, Redwood issues one-time credit equal to pilot discount differential and reverts routing.

2) Feature map: can you provide a single-line table mapping the three items we care about (private VPC, audit retention 13 months, extended KV limits) to whether they are included, addon, or limited on Slate?

Procurement is looped on this thread (procurement@surgetech.com) and will need the MAP and the feature map to proceed to SOW/Docusign.

Heather
